Florida: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open Florida on the map

Key dates

  • Voter registration deadline: October 5, 2026. Last day to register to vote for the November 3, 2026 general election.
  • Last day to request a mail ballot: October 22, 2026. Requests to have a ballot mailed are due by 5 p.m. Mail ballots must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day.
  • Early voting (mandatory statewide period): October 24, 2026 to October 31, 2026. Counties may add optional early voting days. Some counties, such as Pinellas and Palm Beach, hold early voting from October 19 to November 1. Check with your county Supervisor of Elections for sites and hours.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time. Voters must vote at their assigned precinct.

Official election information: Florida Division of Elections

Who's running

Only the U.S. Senate and governor races are loaded so far. Other statewide offices, ballot measures, U.S. House and local races aren't loaded yet. Check your sample ballot for the full list.

Federal

United States Senator

This is a special election to fill the rest of the term that Marco Rubio won in 2022, which ends in January 2029. Ashley Moody was appointed to the seat in January 2025 and is running to keep it.

Names come from the state's official candidate list. Check your sample ballot for the exact party labels.

State

Governor and Lieutenant Governor

This is an open seat for a four-year term because Governor Ron DeSantis is term-limited. Candidates run on joint tickets. The running mates are: Donalds–Bryan Avila, Jolly–Gwen Graham, Jewett–Nicole Skelly, Abrams–Joe Van Vactor, Burkett–Ruben A. Coto, Datto–Juan Santana, Dimanche–Benjiman Rojas, and Russo–Rachel Rodriguez.
